questions.why: The validation checks are validity, consistency, completeness and realism. Refactoring and sprinting are agile terms, and elicitation is a different requirements engineering activity.

questions.text: Closed interviews are based on:
questions.why: Closed interviews use a pre-determined list of questions. Open interviews have no agenda and explore issues freely. In practice interviews are normally a mixture of both.

questions.text: The official statement of what is required of the system developers is the:
questions.why: The software requirements document (SRS) is the official statement of what is required of the system developers. It includes both the user requirements and the system requirements.

questions.text: Which is a requirements validation technique?
questions.why: Requirements reviews (a systematic manual analysis of the requirements) and prototyping are the two validation techniques in the lecture. The other options belong to other areas.

questions.text: Classify each requirement as functional or non-functional. (part 1 of 3)

items.text: Withdrawing money from the bank account.
Completion of a transaction in less than 1 second.
Verifying the bank balance.
Extending the system by providing more tellers for customers.
The system shall generate monthly sales reports including total revenue and customer summaries.
The system shall be available 99.9% of the time.

questions.why: A functional requirement is a service or action the system performs (verb + noun). A non-functional requirement is a quality or constraint on the system, such as speed, availability, capacity, security, usability, legal rules or the development process.

questions.text: Classify each requirement as functional or non-functional. (part 2 of 3)

items.text: A student can register in a course.
The system shall support 10,000 concurrent users.
The system sends an e-mail notification when a reserved book is ready for pickup.
All passwords must be stored in encrypted form.
The interface should be easy to use for novice users.
Upgrading the hardware should be done within 3 hours.

questions.why: Registering and notifying are services the system performs. Capacity, security, usability and a time limit on hardware upgrades are qualities or constraints, so they are non-functional.

questions.text: Classify each requirement as functional or non-functional. (part 3 of 3)

items.text: The customer can cancel his registration.
The system must comply with national data-protection laws.
Each staff member shall be uniquely identified by an eight-digit employee number.
The system shall be developed using the Java language.
The system shall generate each day a list of patients expected to attend appointments.

questions.why: Cancelling a registration and generating a daily list are services. Legal compliance and the choice of programming language are constraints. In the lecture, the eight-digit employee number is listed as a functional requirement (an identification service).

questions.text: Classify each non-functional requirement as product, organizational or external. (part 1 of 2)

items.text: The system must process at least 100 transactions per second.
The system must follow the company's coding standards.
The system must comply with national privacy legislation.
The system must fail no more than once per 1000 hours of operation.
The customer's policy requires the project to be delivered with an agile process.

questions.why: Product requirements describe how the delivered product must behave (speed, reliability, usability). Organizational requirements come from the policies and procedures of the customer's or developer's organization. External requirements come from outside, such as laws and regulations.

questions.text: Classify each non-functional requirement as product, organizational or external. (part 2 of 2)

items.text: The system must interoperate with the existing national ID system.
The user interface must be usable by novices.
The system must respect medical-ethics regulations.
The system must be implemented in the language mandated by the company development policy.
The login screen must load in under 1 second.

questions.why: Interoperability with other systems and ethics regulations come from outside the project. A company-mandated language is organizational policy. Usability and load time describe the delivered product.

questions.text: Classify each person or group by stakeholder type.

items.text: The hospital board that pays for the work.
Medical receptionists who use the system every day.
Testers and software engineers building the system.
Marketing people.
Training personnel involved in the project.

questions.why: System owners pay for the work, end users use the system, and project groups are the people involved in developing it. External stakeholders are outside the organization, for example the government or marketing people.

questions.text: Classify each description as user requirements (BRS) or system requirements (SRS).

items.text: A structured document with detailed descriptions of functions, services and operational constraints.
Defines what should be implemented.
Focuses on what the system should do for the users.

questions.why: User requirements (BRS) describe, from the user's view, what the system should do. System requirements (SRS) are the detailed, structured specification of what should be implemented.

questions.text: Classify each question or problem under the validation check it belongs to.

items.text: Are there any conflicts between requirements?
Are all functions required by the customer included?
Does the system provide the functions that best support the customer's needs?
The 'print report' function that the customer needs was left out.
A requirement needs a technology that does not exist yet.

questions.why: Validity asks whether these are the right functions. Consistency asks whether any requirements conflict. Completeness asks whether anything is missing. Realism asks whether it can be built with the budget and technology available.
